rv.q: It's a testament to the artistry of this production that it makes the play so assuredly agreeable.
But it is as artificial as a plastic topiary, and the farce feels underpowered, like a pillow fight waged with very small pillows.
This London Assurance is a tasty affair where social satire is secondary to laughter.
Fair enough but, with all that wearying plot, enchantment isn't in the cards.
The play’s ingénues seem less, well, assured.
Charlotte Moore has found the right formula to pull this tricky kind of comedy off with her assured production.

cn.t: This handsome revival of Boucicault's 1841 farce offers pleasant period pleasures, though critics find the creaky plot machinery hasn't aged well. The production is deft and cheerful but can't fully overcome the play's antiquated contrivances.
